items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
Presentation from Aird & Berlis LLP - Code of Conduct
notes:
John Mascarin, Aird & Berlis LLP, provided a presentation on the role of the Integrity Commissioner, codes of conduct, and Council/staff roles and responsibilities in the lead up to the presentation of a new code for the Region. He highlighted that the provincial Integrity Commissioner has recommended that the province create a code of conduct for all municipalities, but encouraged the Region to move forward with a new code rather than wait for potential action that may not happen.

J. Mascarin explained the special status of codes of conduct and noted that the new code will apply to both Councillors and citizen appointees to advisory committees, etc. He covered subject matters that are mandatory for a municipality to have in its code, what is included in a complaint protocol and how complaints are handled, as well as the roles and responsibilities of Councillors and staff.

In reply to a question from Council, J. Mascarin clarified that a Chair could expel a Member of Council from a meeting at their own discretion, and this cannot be challenged. J. Mascarin noted that if a Councillor does not think a staff report is complete, the Councillor must ask staff questions in a respectful manner; they are not permitted to cross examine a staff member. He further explained that Councillors can raise questions privately or in a closed session meeting. J. Mascarin noted the power imbalance between Council and staff, but specified that staff have limitations on how they can respond to Council. He stressed that Councillors can ask staff to reconsider and can make amendments to the recommendation.

Replying to a question from Council, J. Mascarin clarified that certain case law indicates that a declared pecuniary interest must exist on the day that the decision is made. A member cannot vote or seek to influence before during or after.

motions.item_title: Motion to go into Closed Session
motions.text: That a closed meeting of Council be held on Wednesday, October 23, 2024 immediately following the Special Council meeting in the Waterloo County Room, in accordance with Section 239 of the “Municipal Act, 2001”, for the purposes of considering the following subject matters: Receiving advice that is subject to solicitor-client privilege related to a proposed purchase of property in Wilmot Township; Providing direction to staff with respect to ongoing negotiations related to a proposed purchase of land; Receiving advice that is subject to solicitor-client privilege related to a potential purchase of property in the City of Cambridge; Providing direction to staff regarding personal matters about identifiable individuals and labour relations related to the potential transfer of a program; Receiving advice that is subject to solicitor-client privilege related to a challenge to a Regional by-law; and Receiving advice that is subject to solicitor-client privilege related to ongoing litigation before the Ontario Land Tribunal.

That a closed meeting of Council be held on Wednesday, October 23, 2024 immediately following the Special Council meeting in the Waterloo County Room, in accordance with Section 239 of the “Municipal Act, 2001”, for the purposes of considering the following subject matters:

  1. Receiving advice that is subject to solicitor-client privilege related to a proposed purchase of property in Wilmot Township;
  2. Providing direction to staff with respect to ongoing negotiations related to a proposed purchase of land;
  3. Receiving advice that is subject to solicitor-client privilege related to a potential purchase of property in the City of Cambridge;
  4. Providing direction to staff regarding personal matters about identifiable individuals and labour relations related to the potential transfer of a program;
  5. Receiving advice that is subject to solicitor-client privilege related to a challenge to a Regional by-law; and
  6. Receiving advice that is subject to solicitor-client privilege related to ongoing litigation before the Ontario Land Tribunal.
